Smt. Premlata Saklecha vs Mangilal on 5 January, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:37678

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Alok Awasthi
 Misc. Appeal No. 71 of 2008

Smt. Premlata Saklecha And Others
 Versus
 Mangilal And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Kailash Chandra Kaushal, Advocate for the appell
 Shri Kunjan Mittal, Advocate for the respondent Nos.1
 Shri Abhay Jain, Advocate for the respondent No.3.
 Heard on : 18.12.2025
 Pronounced on : 05.01.2026
 Judgement

This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') is preferred by the appellants (owner and driver of the offending tractor-trolley)
challenging the impugned award dated 01.11.2007 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Agar (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 18/2006, whereby the respondents No.1 and 2 (claimants-parents of the deceased) have been awarded compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum, and the liability for payment has been fastened jointly and severally upon the driver and owner of the vehicle, while exonerating respondent No.4/Insurance Company from its liability.
The respondent No.3, who is brother of the deceased being not dependent
, his claim has been rejected.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37678 2 MA-71-2008 2.

The brief facts are that on 10.06.2006, at 12.30 PM, the deceased Babulal, aged about 18 years, a mine labourer earning Rs.4,000/- per month (Rs.3,000/- from mining work and Rs.1,000/- from agriculture), was travelling in the trolley attached to the tractor bearing registration No. MP- 13-K-5658-59 alongwith co-workers.
The tractor-trolley was loaded with gravel from the mines.
Due to rash and negligent driving by the appellant- driver, the deceased fell from the trolley onto the road, and the trolley wheel ran over his back, causing fatal injuries, due to which he died.
3. The claimants (parents and brother of the deceased) filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking Rs.10,00,000/- as compensation.

The Tribunal, after appreciating the evidence,
held the driver negligent, awarded Rs.2,00,000/- as compensation, but exonerated the Insurance Smt. Premlata Saklecha vs Mangilal on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57180479/

sentences.text: 1 Company on the grounds that (i) the vehicle was insured only for agricultural purposes, whereas it was used for transporting gravel (non- agricultural/mining purpose), constituting breach of policy conditions; and (ii) the deceased was a gratuitous passenger in the trolley, whose risk was not covered under the policy as no extra premium was paid for passengers.

4. The appellants challenged only the exoneration of the insurance company, contending that the Tribunal erred in holding the use as non- agricultural, and that the policy covered the risk of labourers/passengers as extra premium was paid.
The claimants support the award on liability but submit that the quantum is meager.
The insurance company supports the exoneration, reiterating breach of policy terms and non-coverage of gratuitous passengers.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37678 3 MA-71-2008 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record, including the insurance policy and evidence.
6. On quantum: The deceased was 18 years old, earning Rs.4,000/- per month as proved.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.2,00,000/-, which is indeed meager considering the young age and income.

However, as no cross-appeal or cross-objection has been filed by the claimants for enhancement,
this Court cannot interfere with the quantum in an appeal preferred only by the owner/driver challenging liability.
7.

On liability of the insurance company: The evidence on record, including eyewitness accounts and site plan, establishes that the deceased was travelling in the trolley as a labourer/passenger while gravel was being transported from the mines.

The policy is an 'Act only' policy for the tractor,
specified for agricultural purposes.
Transporting gravel for mining is undisputedly a non-agricultural/commercial purpose, constituting a fundamental breach of policy conditions.
Further, even assuming no breach on use, the deceased was a gratuitous passenger in a goods-carrying vehicle (tractor-trolley used as goods carriage).

As held by the Constitution Bench of the Apex Court in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Asha Rani [(2003) 2 SCC 223], followed in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Balakrishnan [(2013) 1 SCC 731] and several subsequent judgements, an insurer is not liable to cover the risk of gratuitous passengers in a goods vehicle under Section 147 of the Act, as no statutory liability exists for such passengers unless extra premium is paid specifically for the same.

In view of the above, the appeal is devoid of merit and hence, dismissed.
The impugned award dated 01.11.2007 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Agar, is upheld.
The appellants (owner and driver) shall remain jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount with interest as directed.
No order as to costs.
